text:
oliver: Heads up — after the v8 token-splitter rollout I'm seeing a P99 latency jump on the embedder route. p95 is fine, p99 up ~140ms vs baseline. Grafana panels linked: https://graf.redwood/graf/ABCD/embedder-latency :eyes:

maya: Can you paste the exact query and time window? also which canary fraction?

oliver: Query = `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum(rate(request_duration_bucket[5m])) by (le, route))` window 10m. Canary was 5% starting 2026-03-18T10:00Z, spike started ~10:12Z.

deploy-bot: service.deploy: rollout v8-token-splitter -> canary (5% nodes) started at 2026-03-18T10:00:00Z.

sam: My gut: tokenizer produced more subtokens for common prompts -> prefetcher overfetch + KV cache miss rate up -> batcher sees more variable seq lengths and kernel-decider flips to slower kernel more often. That combination can hit p99 without changing p95.

ineesha: Ran a quick cpu/profile dump on a canary node. Top stacks show heavy time in `prefetcher::fetch_prefix` and `kernel_mux::choose_slow_path`. Snapshot (truncated):
```
  30% prefetcher::fetch_prefix
  22% kvcache::lookup_miss
  18% kernel_mux::choose_slow_path
  10% batcher::flush_with_backpressure
  5% allocator::page_evict
```
kv-hit ratio in the snapshot window: 68% (baseline 92%).

li: Host-level metrics: one host in the canary pool had GPU memory pressure (~90%) and a competing tenant that triggered eviction. Evictions correlate with the largest p99 buckets. Kernel-decider logs show repeated `fallback_to_generic_kernel` for the embedder model.

jordy: Reproduced locally with subset of production prompts. Command: `./perf_run --model v8-token-split --seed=prod-sample --workers=8 --seqdist=prod.json`. Result: p99 increased from 85ms -> 220ms, CPU/GPU stalls visible.

maya: I think we should pause canary and route traffic away from the affected hosts. Also add a temporary policy to prefer dedicated-capacity routing for embedder until we have a fix. @deploy-bot can you pause? :thumbsup:

deploy-bot: service.deploy: canary paused at 2026-03-18T10:24:31Z. Canary traffic drained from 5% -> 0% over ~90s.

sam: Short-term mitigation: tighten kernel-decider thresholds so seq-length variance doesn't trigger slow-path fallback prematurely, and reduce prefetcher aggressiveness for token-splitter variants. Patch idea:
```yaml
kernel_decider:
  slow_path_threshold: 0.75  # was 0.6
  seq_variance_window: 120s

prefetcher:
  max_prefetch_tokens: 16  # was 64 for v8 token-split
  kv_lookup_batch: 32
```
This should reduce unnecessary kernel flips and KV churn while we investigate tokenizer changes.

ineesha: I'll prepare a canary hotfix with those config changes + a kvcache metric instrument (kv_hit/kv_miss tags). Planning test run in staging now.

oliver: Thanks. Priorities: (1) keep traffic stable (done), (2) push hotfix to canary/staging and validate p99 + kv-hit, (3) deep dive on tokenization diffs vs v7 to see why subtokens increased.

li: I'll also isolate the noisy neighbor host from the canary pool and check eviction policies — may need stricter host isolation for canaries.

jordy: adding a perf regression ticket and linking repro artifacts here: https://tickets.redwood/PR-5234. Attachments: perf traces, sample prompts.

sam: if hotfix looks good we can roll config to canary at 1% first and watch p99/kvcache for 30m.

oliver: Good plan. @ineesha @sam please post results here after staging run. I'll keep an eye on alerts and our SLO dashboard. :eyes:
